# DESIGN.md — Marigold

archetype: warm-trattoria
rationale: Marigold is a named-chef, Forbes-covered neighborhood Indian restaurant in Eastchester — it sells on warmth, story and credibility, not on speed or price; warm-trattoria gives it the textured, human, unpretentious quality the tagline "neighborhood spot for good food and moments worth sharing" earns, without the clinical minimalism of editorial-fine-dining or the flat-colour loudness of bold-fast-casual that would undercut Chef Ravi's Michelin credentials.
interaction_level: L2

personality: [warm, confident, rooted, inviting]

typography:
  display: "Barlow"
  body: "Barlow"
  scale: 1.250
  notes: >
    Barlow is the brand font throughout. Display headings at 700–800 weight, condensed where
    space is tight (hero headline, section eyebrows). Body at 400, 1rem, 1.65 leading.
    Category eyebrows in Barlow 600 small-caps, letter-spaced 0.12em. Prices in 700,
    never below 0.9rem. Subheadings step 1.25× down from display; captions at 0.8rem 400.
    Weight does the typographic work — only the hero headline breaks 3rem; the rest of the
    scale stays considered and close, not shouted.

palette:
  primary: "#0D4948"
  secondary: "#FF6A00"
  accent: "#FF462D"
  ground: "#F5F0EB"
  surface: "#FFFFFF"
  ink: "#0D2B2A"
  muted: "#5A6E6C"
  border: "#D6CFC7"
  application: >
    Primary (#0D4948) carries the header, footer, the hours-and-location band, and the main
    reservation CTA — structural teal, present everywhere the page commits weight. Secondary
    (#FF6A00) is the warmth signal: category eyebrow rules, the Happy Hour band, the "Book
    your table today" button on hover/active, and the phone number set as a tel link.
    Accent (#FF462D) appears exactly once — the oversized opening quotation mark on the
    pulled review — earning its heat at a single moment. Ground (#F5F0EB) is a warm
    flour-toned off-white drawn from the marigold flower's warmth; it separates every page
    from a generic white restaurant site and is never substituted with pure white.
    Surface (#FFFFFF) lifts the menu listing panel and the nav off the ground. Ink (#0D2B2A)
    is the primary teal pushed to near-black, keeping all body text tonally within the brand.
    Muted (#5A6E6C) for descriptions, captions, secondary labels — verified ≥ 4.5:1 against
    ground and surface. Border (#D6CFC7) for hairline rules between menu items and section
    dividers. Every neutral derives from the teal-and-warm-paper axis; no generic grey ramp
    appears anywhere.

composition:
  whitespace: balanced
  photography: supporting
  card_usage: minimal
  mobile: >
    Hero crops to 16:9, headline stacks above the image rather than over it at 2.2rem,
    button goes full-width below the text block. Menu page uses grouped-accordion (one
    category open at a time). Happy Hour band stacks to full-width single column. Gallery
    collapses to a 2-column grid of 4:3 crops. Hours and address stack vertically; no map
    embed (embed URL not available). Sticky-bar appears on mobile only with the reservation
    CTA. Nav collapses to a hamburger opening a full-height primary-coloured drawer with
    primary links and the reservation action.

composition: >
  The homepage makes one argument: this is a real neighborhood place with serious culinary
  credentials, and you should book a table tonight. Lead with atmosphere — a full-bleed food
  photograph and the Marigold name answer "what is this?" in three seconds. Before the visitor
  scrolls past the fold, give them the Forbes recognition and the Michelin-chef line, because
  that credential is the single fact that separates Marigold from every other Indian restaurant
  in Eastchester and it has to land early. The menu is 105 items and belongs on its own page,
  but the homepage must gesture at it with eight items showing the full price spread ($12–$34)
  so visitors know what to expect without leaving. Happy Hour earns a loud flat-colour band
  because it answers a real same-evening decision — it belongs where the visitor is actively
  considering whether to come in. The gallery of real food photographs builds kitchen confidence
  without a word of copy. Chef Ravi's story appears because this is a destination with a named
  chef and press coverage — the human story is why someone chooses this room over the block
  away. Close on hours, address and one reservation button; never bury the hours on mobile.
  The page holds back the full menu, the full specials list, the party and catering enquiry
  forms — all of those live on their own pages, signposted clearly from here.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Place Marigold as a specific, confident destination — modern Indian cooking in Eastchester
      by a named chef — and put one clear action (reserve a table) in front of the visitor within
      three seconds of landing.
    spec: >
      Full-bleed photograph of plated food (use
      https://deveusblob.blob.core.windows.net/kora-business-images/user-media/1e9b79ec-53a2-4b94-836f-c653e96b0c4e/65b77bab-5ae0-4018-9139-f16544fc950f/1792066183_szidlz.webp),
      dark gradient from bottom-left to transparent upper-right at no more than 0.45 opacity
      so the food reads clearly. Marigold logo top-left in the nav. Headline "Modern Indian.
      Neighborhood Heart." in Barlow 800 condensed at 4rem, white, flush-left in the
      lower-left third of the frame. Beneath it the tagline "Neighborhood spot for good food
      and moments worth sharing" in Barlow 400 at 1.1rem, white, same alignment. One button
      "Book your table today" in secondary (#FF6A00) with white text, flush-left beneath the
      tagline, linking to /eastchester-marigold-reservations. No secondary button, no social
      icons in the frame. On mobile: image crops to 16:9, headline drops to 2.2rem, button
      full-width below the text block, image sits above the text not behind it.

  - id: awards
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Answer "is this place worth it?" before the visitor scrolls far — Forbes coverage and
      a Michelin-chef credential are the most persuasive facts Marigold has, and they must
      appear high on the page while the visitor is still forming an impression.
    spec: >
      A narrow full-width band in primary (#0D4948). Two awards in a single row on desktop,
      stacked on mobile. Left: "Michelin Chef" in Barlow 700 small-caps white, a short
      accent-coloured (#FF462D) rule above it, nothing else. Right: publication name "Forbes"
      in Barlow 700 white at 0.8rem letter-spaced, then "One of the Best in the Tri-State
      Region" in Barlow 400 white at 0.95rem beneath. No badge clip-art, no rosette SVGs,
      no decorative borders — text and rules only. A border-colour hairline separates the
      band from the hero above and the next section below. On mobile both awards stack
      vertically, centred, 1rem gap.

  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: "8 of 105, chosen for range, links to eastchester-marigold-food-menu.html"
    intent: >
      Show the visitor what Marigold serves and what it costs across the full spread —
      starters to premium mains — so they can self-qualify, then send them to the full
      menu page for everything.
    spec: >
      Section eyebrow "A taste of what's inside" in Barlow 600 small-caps muted,
      letter-spaced, above heading "On the Menu" in Barlow 700 at 2rem ink, flush-left.
      Eight items in two columns on desktop, one on mobile: Samosa Trio ($13), Baigan
      Burrata ($12), Achari Chicken Tikka ($14), Butter Chicken ($24), Goat Biryani ($27),
      Tandoori Shrimp ($30), Lamb Chops ($34), Vegetable Biryani ($22). Each item: name
      in Barlow 600 ink, description in muted 0.875rem beneath, price right-aligned on the
      same baseline as the name with a dotted leader between — no images, no card borders,
      no rounded corners, only a hairline border-colour rule between items. Below the grid,
      a text link "View full menu →" in secondary (#FF6A00) Barlow 600, centred, linking to
      /eastchester-marigold-food-menu. Note in muted beneath: "For food allergies, please
      speak to your server." On mobile, single column, link becomes a full-width secondary
      button.

  - id: offers
    priority: essential
    show: "2 of 7, chosen for immediacy, links to eastchester-marigold-happy-hours-specials.html"
    intent: >
      Give the visitor a concrete reason to come in tonight — Happy Hour is a genuine
      weekday differentiator and the Early Bird covers weekend traffic; both must be
      unmissable and set in terms a visitor can act on immediately.
    spec: >
      A full-width flat band in secondary (#FF6A00) with white type — the page's one
      loud moment and its distinctive visual beat. Left half desktop: label "HAPPY HOUR"
      in Barlow 800 condensed uppercase white at 3rem; times "Mon–Thu · 4:30–6:30 PM" in
      Barlow 600 white at 1.1rem; offer line "Appetizers $7 · Cocktails & Beers Half Price"
      in Barlow 400 white at 1rem. Right half desktop: "Early Bird Special" in Barlow 700
      white at 1.5rem; "3 Courses + Champagne Toast — $40" in Barlow 600 white at 1.1rem;
      "Sat & Sun · 11:30 AM–3 PM" in Barlow 400 white at 0.9rem. A single vertical white
      hairline at 40% opacity divides the two halves. White text link "See all specials →"
      right-aligned beneath the right panel, linking to
      /eastchester-marigold-happy-hours-specials. On mobile: stacks vertically, each offer
      full-width, divider becomes a horizontal rule, link full-width centred beneath.

  - id: gallery
    priority: supporting
    show: "8 of 12"
    intent: >
      Let the kitchen speak before the story section — eight real food photographs give the
      visitor sensory confidence in what they are about to read about.
    spec: >
      A filmstrip on a ground-coloured band: eight images cropped to 4:3, horizontally
      scrollable on desktop with overflow-x scroll, clipped at both edges to imply
      continuation, no arrows, touch-scrollable. Images edge-to-edge with a 4px gap, no
      borders, no captions, no rounded corners. Use the eight gallery URLs from the provided
      image list verbatim. On mobile, collapses to a 2-column grid of 4:3 crops, all eight
      visible. No section heading — the photographs carry this position without one.

  - id: reviews
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Convert the visitor who is almost convinced — four named, specific five-star reviews
      (Tandoori chicken, staff warmth, the chef's palette) provide the social proof that
      closes the decision for a neighborhood restaurant.
    spec: >
      Mina Oza's review as the hero quote: text at 1.6rem Barlow 400 italic ink, max-measure
      640px, centred on a surface (#FFFFFF) panel with generous vertical padding. Attribution
      "— Mina Oza" in Barlow 600 small-caps muted beneath; no star graphic. An oversized
      accent-coloured (#FF462D) opening quotation mark at 5rem sits above the text as the
      sole decorative element — the page's one use of the accent. Below, the remaining three
      reviews (Ryma I, Bella M, Grumpy G) in a single row of three plain text columns on
      desktop, stacked single column on mobile. Each column: author name in Barlow 600 ink;
      five plain filled circles in secondary (#FF6A00) beside the name at 0.6rem; review text
      in Barlow 400 0.9rem muted. Columns separated by border-colour hairline rules. No card
      borders, no drop shadows, no rounded corners anywhere in this section.

  - id: story
    priority: supporting
    show: all
    intent: >
      Earn the premium positioning — a Forbes-covered Michelin chef with a regional Indian
      cooking range deserves more than a paragraph; this section is why a visitor chooses
      Marigold over the Indian restaurant two blocks away.
    spec: >
      Magazine-column on desktop: right-side image (use
      https://deveusblob.blob.core.windows.net/kora-business-images/user-media/1e9b79ec-53a2-4b94-836f-c653e96b0c4e/65b77bab-5ae0-4018-9139-f16544fc950f/1792066194_8fmfdv.png)
      bleeding to the page right edge; text column occupying the left 55%, max-measure 560px.
      Eyebrow "Our Story" in Barlow 600 small-caps secondary, letter-spaced. Heading "Chef
      Ravi — Bringing Authentic Indian Cuisine to Your Table" in Barlow 700 at 2rem ink.
      Body in Barlow 400 1rem ink: three short paragraphs covering the founding belief, Chef
      Ravi's background and regional range (North, South, East, West), and what sets the
      kitchen apart — tandoori technique, hand-rolled breads, inclusive dietary options. One
      secondary-coloured text link "Read more about us →" linking to
      /eastchester-marigold-about-us. On mobile: image full-width above, text full-width
      below, standard single-column flow.

  - id: hours_location
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Remove the last practical obstacle — a visitor who wants to come needs hours and address
      readable in under five seconds, without hunting through any other section.
    spec: >
      Stacked-band in primary (#0D4948), white type throughout. Two equal columns on desktop.
      Left: heading "Hours" Barlow 700 white 1.25rem; each day-range and its hours as a
      two-column aligned pair (day-range left, hours right) in Barlow 400 white 0.95rem,
      hairline white 20%-opacity rule between rows. Exact hours from the content:
      Monday–Thursday 11:30 am–3 pm then 4:30 pm–10:00 pm; Friday & Saturday 11:30 am–10 pm;
      Sunday 11:30 am–9:30 pm. Right: heading "Find Us" Barlow 700 white 1.25rem; address
      "434 White Plains Road Eastchester, NY 10709" Barlow 400 white; phone "(914) 202-9455"
      Barlow 600 white as a tel: link; email "info@marigold.restaurant" Barlow 400 white as a
      mailto: link. No map embed (no embed URL available). One white outline button "Book your
      table today" linking to /eastchester-marigold-reservations below the address column.
      On mobile: stacks vertically, hours first then address, button full-width.

  - id: cta
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: >
      Close the page on one clear action — a visitor who has scrolled to the bottom is ready;
      one button and one phone number, nothing else.
    spec: >
      Quiet-close band on ground (#F5F0EB). Centred heading "Ready to join us?" in Barlow 700
      ink at 1.75rem. One line of muted body text "Reservations recommended — we'd love to
      see you." One primary-coloured (#0D4948) button "Book your table today" linking to
      /eastchester-marigold-reservations, white text Barlow 600. Below the button, phone number
      "(914) 202-9455" in Barlow 600 secondary (#FF6A00) as a tel: link. Nothing else in the
      band. On mobile: button full-width, same centred layout.

avoid:
  - A centred hero with three icon-and-label cards beneath it ("Fresh · Local · Authentic" or any variant)
  - Drop-shadow or rounded-corner cards on any menu listing or review
  - Sepia, warm-filtered or darkened photography overlays that obscure the actual food
  - A photograph beside every menu item — none exist and placeholders are worse than no image
  - Star-rating SVG graphics anywhere — use plain filled circles or text attribution only
  - The word "artisan" as a standalone descriptor for the cuisine
  - An auto-playing carousel or slideshow for reviews or gallery images
  - Generic stock photography of any kind — only the twelve provided URLs
  - Burying the Happy Hour details below the fold on mobile
  - Any nav item pointing to a page this site does not serve (no "Drink Menu", no "Events")
  - A floating pill-shaped "Book Now" button overlaid on the hero photograph
  - Thin geometric sans headings or cold grey neutrals — warm-trattoria warmth must come through
  - A "Fresh · Local · Homemade" or equivalent three-column icon grid anywhere on the page
  - Any invented FAQ section — there is no FAQ content and the section does not exist
